practiceNotes: Recall practice should maintain definitions, representations, assumptions, mechanism steps, diagnostic signatures and method-selection criteria; it does not replace assessed construction or investigation.
Assess proofs through complete arguments and counterexamples; assess programming through executable artifacts, adversarial tests, reproducibility and explanation of complexity or numerical error.

Laboratory and field work requires appropriate facilities, training, supervision and local risk approval. Use safe substitutes or archived data when access is unavailable; this does not certify hands-on competence.
Human-participant studies, identifiable biological data, vertebrate work, environmental sampling and genetic manipulation require applicable consent, authorization and ethics review.
Cybersecurity practice must use owned or explicitly authorized isolated systems. Distributed-system fault injection must not affect operational services.
Radiation, lasers, high voltage, pressure systems, cryogens and hazardous chemicals require specialist supervision and approved procedures; the curriculum does not confer operating authorization.
Biological culture work should use approved low-risk organisms. Clinical reasoning projects use de-identified or synthetic cases and do not authorize diagnosis or treatment.

Provided scientific software may be used only where the contract teaches model specification, inputs, diagnostics and limitations; algorithm implementation and theorem proving are assessed separately when explicitly promised.
Use unfamiliar transfer problems, cumulative projects and delayed reassessment. Preserve laboratory notebooks, code versions, uncertainty budgets and negative results as evidence of competence.

scopeIssues: Graduate systems biology and computational neuroscience currently share biology/systems-biology. Its earliest reaction-network and flux-balance tasks unnecessarily require the complete biology/neuroscience and animal-physiology ancestry; these working capabilities need a separate accessible quantitative-cellular destination connected to the neural continuation.

Graduate stochastic-process theory in mathematics/stochastic-processes currently requires numerical methods and differential equations for every learner, although its first measure-theoretic probability and Markov-chain tasks do not need that preparation. A separate probability/process foundation and connected stochastic-calculus continuation are needed.

Undergraduate computational physics in physics/computational-physics imposes optimization and statistical inference on first forward-simulation tasks. The forward simulation and field-solver route should be separated from the inverse-modeling continuation.

chemistry/advanced-inorganic-chemistry promises kinetic discrimination of catalytic mechanisms but does not require chemistry/kinetics or locally teach rate-law derivation and fitting. Its graduate catalytic-inference preparation remains insufficient.

The current inventory does not yet provide independently assessable graduate algebraic geometry or analytic/algebraic number-theory foundations beyond elementary number theory and graduate algebra; these established mathematical continuations remain unfinished.

Established working and graduate foundations for computer vision, robotics/control and information theory are not independently specified. Graphics, classical AI, optimization and signal analysis do not by themselves teach their distinctive inverse-inference, state-estimation and coding methods.
The coverage inventory lacks matching deferred rows for the unfinished mathematical and computing domains identified above; those domains must not be treated as available preparation.
